title: Three to one against
hook: The bookie says 3 to 1 against. What chance of winning does that actually mean?

knows: a chance as a share of all equally likely outcomes
doesNotKnow: that odds compare wins with losses, not wins with everything

misconception: "3 to 1 against" means a 1-in-3 (33%) chance of winning.
objective: The learner can turn odds of L to W against into a chance of W / (W + L), and explains that 3 to 1 against is 1 in 4 (25%).
keyState: 3 blocks in Lose and 1 in Win (odds 3 to 1 against, win chance 1 of 4 = 25%), then 2 and 2 (evens, 50%).

claims.text: Odds of L to W against mean L losses for every W wins; the lesson reads "3 to 1 against" this way, as bookmakers' fractional odds 3/1 do.
claims.source: Betting convention for fractional odds (e.g. 3/1 = 3 to 1 against). Bookmakers' quoted odds also include a profit margin, so their implied chances add to more than 100%; the lesson uses odds as a plain ratio of outcomes.

claims.text: The chance of a win is wins divided by all outcomes: W / (W + L).
claims.source: Definition of probability over equally likely outcomes; chance() in src/demos/probability/odds-three-to-one/Demo.tsx.

claims.text: 3 to 1 against is a win chance of 1 of 4 = 25%, not 1 in 3 (33%).
Odds of 2 to 2 are the same as 1 to 1 ("evens"): a 50% chance.
claims.source: 2 / (2 + 2) = 0.5. "Evens" is the betting name for 1 to 1.

claims.text: Odds of 4 to 1 against are a 1 in 5 (20%) chance (recall question).

recall.question: A team is at odds of 4 to 1 against. What chance of winning does that imply?
recall.why: 4 to 1 against is 4 losses for every 1 win: 1 win out of 5 outcomes, so 20%. 25% would divide wins by losses.
